adaptation: Copied model definitions, removed repository imports, replaced dataset/batch orchestration and output adapters. Source low-rate GP/LDBLL budgets retained; fixed epochs replace validation/early stopping.
adaptation_details: Dataset formula from arXiv:2505.18526v1 section 4.1; no DBK implementation.
Original standalone model and mathematical definitions copied with repository imports removed.
Independent per-head batches, source initialization, losses and predictive distributions retained.
Shared synthetic artifact replaces tabular split loading; no validation/test-based model selection.
GP early stopping disabled and LDBLL validation selection replaced by fixed source maximum budgets.
Deep ensemble may reuse a matching original BDKN first-stage checkpoint; repulsive checkpoints are rejected.
CPU threads default to one for small matrices; output adapters add plotting, scoring and serialization.
VBLL script named vbll_regression.py to avoid shadowing the external vbll library.
LDBLL prints progress every 1,000 epochs without changing training operations.
User requested LDBLL 500 epochs to match the other neural methods, replacing its 30,000-epoch source budget.
Latest user-requested training budget: 2,000 epochs for every method, including GP and LDBLL; Bayesian stages retain 100 optimization steps.
User requested LDBLL learning rate 0.001 and hidden widths [50, 50] to match the other neural methods; existing LDBLL derivative regularization and remaining method settings retained.
DKL and LDBLL now use the user-requested 10,000 epochs; other methods retain 2,000 epochs.
Repulsive ensembles tested at strengths 0.001, 0.01, and 0.1; non-repulsive fits reused across strength comparisons.
CUDA-synchronized fitting timers exclude prediction and plotting; deep-ensemble checkpoint reuse retains its original fitting cost.
Offline report registry supports dataset, neural learning-rate, and repulsion-strength selection.
Additional requested strengths 1 and 10 added. Dedicated unweighted repulsion-loss plots and default logarithmic loss axes; extreme FRDE errors retained with an explicitly labeled data-range zoom.
